items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: The messenger at the Custom House when I was working there in the 1916-17 would occasionally bring me in a piece of music that Williams and Pirone published.

ctx.x: collected dimes on corners or something of that sort. In Chicago in later years they'd go from tavern to tavern. Singers are small instrumental groups, and today you can hear them on Halstead Street and some of the places where there are open air markets. Set up a loudspeaker and a guitar. The one thing I remember

close to that is that at the corner Canal and Rampart Street there used to be a small open truck, one of these light delivery trucks with an open wagon. And they had a couple of pieces of music in that, and a Negro standing in the back or sitting in the back singing. They used to give a little concert there on the street like that, but it wasn't like a street singer really. It wasn't Clarence Williams and Pirone trying to sell their music for us. No, I never saw them. The messenger at the Custom House when I was…
Well, I have seen the cover. Have you? Yes. Someone in Chicago has a copy of it, and I think I've seen your... Is that Mr. Hardin or someone by the name? Yes, yes. You know him? Yes.
